en: Paṭisambhidāmagga 3 Paññāvagga 3.3.
Discourse on Realization (Abhisamaya-kathā)
"Full realization":
by what does one realize?
One realizes by means of the mind.
If one realizes through the mind, then does one who lacks knowledge realize?
One who lacks knowledge does not realize; one realizes through knowledge.
If one realizes through knowledge, then does one realize by means of that which is both non-conscious and knowledge?
One does not realize by means of that which is non-conscious and knowledge. One realizes by means of consciousness and knowledge.
If one realizes by means of both mind and knowledge, then does one realize by means of a sense-sphere mind and a sense-sphere knowledge?
One does not realize by means of a sense-sphere mind and a sense-sphere knowledge.
Then, does one realize by means of a fine-material-sphere mind and a fine-material-sphere knowledge?
One does not realize by means of both a fine-material-sphere mind and knowledge.
Does one then realize by means of both an immaterial-sphere mind and knowledge?
One does not realize by means of both an immaterial-sphere mind and knowledge.
In that case, does one realize through a mind that possesses ownership of action and through knowledge?
No, one does not realize through a mind that possesses ownership of action and through knowledge.
In that case, does one realize through a mind that conforms to the truths and through knowledge?
One does not realize through a mind that conforms to truth and through knowledge.
Then, does one realize through a past mind and through knowledge?
One does not realize through a past mind and through knowledge.
In that case, does one realize by means of a future mind and knowledge?
No, one does not realize by means of a future mind and knowledge.
In that case, does one realize by means of a present mundane mind and knowledge?
One does not realize through a present mundane mind and knowledge.
At the moment of the supramundane path, one realizes through a present mind and knowledge.
How does one realize at the moment of the supramundane path through a present mind and knowledge?
At the moment of the supramundane path, the consciousness dominated by arising is both the cause and the condition for knowledge;
and the knowledge associated with it, which has cessation as its object and is dominated by seeing, is both the cause and the condition for that consciousness.
Thus, at the moment of the supramundane path, one realizes through both present consciousness and knowledge.
Is clear realization (abhisamaya) merely this much? No.
At the moment of the supramundane path, right view is the clear realization of seeing; right intention is the clear realization of directing toward.
The breakthrough by means of full comprehension of grasping is right speech; the breakthrough by means of full comprehension of origination is right action;

the breakthrough by means of full comprehension of purification is right livelihood; the breakthrough by means of full comprehension of exertion is right effort; the breakthrough by means of full comprehension of establishment is right mindfulness; the breakthrough by means of full comprehension of non-distraction is right concentration.

The breakthrough by means of full comprehension of establishment is the mindfulness enlightenment factor; the breakthrough by means of full comprehension of investigation is the investigation-of-phenomena enlightenment factor.
The clear comprehension of exertion is the energy enlightenment factor; the clear comprehension of pervasion is the rapture enlightenment factor;

the clear comprehension of tranquility is the tranquility enlightenment factor; the clear comprehension of non-distraction is the concentration enlightenment factor; the clear comprehension of reflective discernment is the equanimity enlightenment factor.
The realization of being unshakable by lack of faith is the power of faith; the realization of being unshakable by laziness is the power of energy;
the realization of being unshakable by negligence is the power of mindfulness; the realization of being unshakable by restlessness is the power of concentration;
the realization of being unshakable by ignorance is the power of wisdom.

The breakthrough by means of resolve is the faculty of faith; the breakthrough by means of exertion is the faculty of energy; the breakthrough by means of establishment is the faculty of mindfulness; the breakthrough by means of non-distraction is the faculty of concentration; the breakthrough by means of seeing is the faculty of wisdom. In the sense of predominance, it is the breakthrough of the faculties;

in the sense of unshakability, it is the breakthrough of the powers; in the sense of outlet, it is the breakthrough of the factors of enlightenment; in the sense of cause, it is the breakthrough of the path;
in the sense of establishment, it is the breakthrough of the foundations of mindfulness; in the sense of striving, it is the breakthrough of the right efforts.

In the sense of succeeding, it is the realization of the bases of success; in the sense of suchness, it is the realization of the truths; in the sense of non-distraction, it is the realization of serenity;
in the sense of contemplation, it is the realization of insight; in the sense of a single flavor, it is the realization of serenity and insight;

in the sense of non-excess, it is the realization of the yoke-pair; in the sense of restraint, it is the realization of purification of virtue; and in the sense of non-distraction, it is the realization of purification.

In the sense of seeing, it is the clear realization of purification of view; in the sense of being freed, it is the clear realization of liberation; in the sense of penetration, it is the clear realization of true knowledge;
in the sense of relinquishment, it is the clear realization of deliverance; in the sense of eradication, the knowledge of destruction is the clear realization.
Zeal is the clear realization in the sense of being the root; attention is the clear realization in the sense of origination; contact is the clear realization in the sense of convergence.
Realization: feeling is realization in the sense of convergence; concentration is realization in the sense of being foremost;
mindfulness is realization in the sense of predominance; wisdom is realization in the sense of being supreme; liberation is realization in the sense of being the essence;
and Nibbāna, which plunges into the deathless, is realization in the sense of the ultimate goal.
Is realization (abhisamaya) only this much?
No. At the moment of the path of stream-entry (sotāpatti-magga), there is the realization of seeing (dassanābhisamaya), which is right view … [and so on] … up to … right concentration.
Nibbāna, which is plunged into the deathless, is the convergence in the sense of being the ultimate end.
Is the convergence merely this much? No, indeed.
At the moment of the fruit of stream-entry, the convergence of vision is right view … [and so on] … the knowledge of non-arising in the sense of subsiding is the convergence.
Zeal is the convergence in the sense of being the root … [and so on] …
Nibbāna, which plunges into the deathless, is the convergence in the sense of being the ultimate end.
Is the convergence merely this much? No, it is not.
At the moment of the path of once-returning … at the moment of the fruit of once-returning … at the moment of the path of non-returning …
At the moment of the fruit of non-returning … at the moment of the path to arahantship … down to … at the moment of the fruit of arahantship,
the convergence of vision is right view; the convergence of directing onto is right intention … down to … [the other factors].
In the sense of subsiding, knowledge of non-arising is convergence.
Zeal is convergence in the sense of being the root ... [and so on] ...
Nibbāna, which plunges into the Deathless, is convergence in the sense of being the culmination.
When one abandons defilements, does one abandon past defilements ... pe ...
does one abandon future defilements, or does one abandon present defilements?

If one abandons past defilements, then does one exhaust what is already exhausted, cause the ceased to cease, cause the vanished to vanish, cause the subsided to subside, and abandon that which is past and non-existent?
"One does not abandon defilements in the past;
one abandons defilements in the future.

If one abandons defilements in the future, then surely one abandons what is unborn, one abandons what is unarisen, one abandons what has not appeared, one abandons what is not manifest, and one abandons that which is in the future and non-existent?
"One does not abandon future defilements;
one abandons present defilements.
"If one abandons present defilements, then surely one who is lustful abandons lust, and one who is hateful abandons hatred."
Does one who is deluded abandon delusion; one who is bound abandon conceit; one who is misapprehending abandon views;
one who has fallen into distraction abandon restlessness; one who has not reached the goal abandon doubt; and one who has become entrenched abandon the underlying tendencies?
Are dark and bright phenomena proceeding in equal balance, such that there is a path-cultivation associated with defilement?
For one does not abandon past defilements, nor does one abandon future defilements, nor does one abandon present defilements.
If one does not abandon past defilements, nor future ones, nor present defilements,
then surely there is no development of the path, no realization of the fruit, no abandoning of defilements, and no penetration of the Dhamma?
There is the development of the path, there is the realization of the fruit, there is the abandoning of the defilements, and there is the breakthrough to the Dhamma. How so?
It is just as if there were a young tree that had not yet borne fruit.
A man might cut its root.

Those fruits of that tree which have not yet been born would not be born while still unborn; those not yet produced would not be produced while still unproduced; those not yet arisen would not arise while still unarisen; those not yet manifested would not become manifest while still unmanifested.
In the same way, arising is the cause, arising is the condition for the production of the defilements.
Seeing the danger in arising, the mind leaps forward into non-arising.
Because the mind leaps forward into non-arising, those defilements that would have arisen through the conditions of arising do not arise even when unarisen;
they do not come into being even when unproduced; they do not emerge even when unmanifested; and they do not become evident even when unapparent.
Thus, with the cessation of the cause, there is the cessation of suffering.
The cause is the process of occurrence, the cause is the sign, and the cause is the accumulation.
Accumulation is the condition for the production of defilements.
Seeing the danger in effort, the mind leaps forward into non-effort.
Because the mind leaps forward into non-effort, those defilements that might have arisen through the condition of effort do not arise even when unarisen;
they do not come into being even when unproduced; they do not emerge even when unmanifested; and they do not become evident even when not yet apparent.
Thus, with the cessation of the cause, there is the cessation of suffering.
Thus, there is the cultivation of the path, there is the realization of the fruit, there is the abandoning of the defilements, and there is the breakthrough to the Dhamma.
The Discussion on Breakthrough is finished.
